subject: Discovery recap & PoC plan — FinPay integration
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Jessie Carter <jessie.carter@finpay.com>, Rajiv Iyer <rajiv.iyer@finpay.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-02-28T15:10:00-08:00
Subject: Discovery recap & PoC plan — FinPay integration

Hi Jessie / Rajiv —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery call and a proposed PoC/onboarding plan so we have alignment going into next week. Please flag anything I missed or that you want adjusted.

High-level business pain & goals
- Reduce average AHT (agent handle time) for billing and dispute tickets by 30% within 3 months.
- Automate entity extraction and routing for reconciliation exceptions to reduce manual work.
- Keep customer PII and payment data within FinPay’s controls (PCI-sensitive).

Current stack (what you described)
- Microservices on AWS EKS (Node.js + Go).
- Front-line customer support: Zendesk via internal connectors.
- Experimental usage of OpenAI for canned responses; costs are growing and you have residency concerns.

Success criteria for the PoC
- Functional: Redwood can perform intent classification, entity extraction, and generate agent suggestions with >80% accuracy on your evaluation set.
- Performance: p50 latency < 250 ms, sustain ~10 concurrent req/s for the chat endpoint.
- Security: Data residency / VPC peering in place and DPA agreed.
- Economics: per-conv cost target ~X (we'll refine once we see token counts).

Proposed PoC & onboarding plan (6-week target)
- Week 0 (this week): Finalize scope, sign PoC SOW / DPA. Owners: Neha (Redwood AE), Jessie (FinPay PM).
- Week 1: Integration kickoff — API keys, sample dataset exchange, enable sandbox access. Owner: Dev (Redwood SE).
- Week 2: Ingest sample tickets, run initial evaluation, iterate prompts and extraction rules.
- Week 3: Add streaming agent suggestions and test latency under load.
- Week 4: Performance tuning (batching, KV cache) and quantization recommendations.
- Week 5: Security review, enable VPC peering (if Private), audit logs validation.
- Week 6: Final review & go/no-go decision.

Technical scope notes (short)
- SDK languages: Python (primary) and TypeScript / Node.
- API compatibility: We support an OpenAI-like chat / completions endpoint, embeddings, and streaming. Function-calling style output available for structured extraction.
- Network: TLS outbound to api.redwood.ai; for Private deployment we support VPC peering and on-prem packages.
- Models: For the PoC we recommend a quantized ~13B variant (cost/perf sweet spot) — will propose exact model IDs once we finalize the evaluation workload.

Attachments: I’m sharing a short integration checklist and the PoC SOW draft for signatures.
[Attachment: finpay-mvp-requirements.pdf] [Attachment: redwood-poc-sla.xlsx] [Attachment: integration-checklist.csv]

Next steps / asks from FinPay
- Share a small evaluation set (5–10 representative tickets) by Mon 3/2.
- Confirm whether you prefer Hosted API sandbox or Private PoC (we can do either; Private needs additional network setup).
- Proposed next meeting: Wed 3/3 11:00 AM PT to kick off integration (please confirm).

Thanks — looking forward to working together.

Neha Kapoor
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0198

Subject: Re: Discovery recap & PoC plan — FinPay integration

Hi Neha —

Thanks for the clear recap. This looks good and aligns with what we discussed. A few quick clarifications:

1) Data residency / compliance: We need a DPA and confirmation that logs containing PII can be turned off or routed to our audit bucket. Can your security team confirm this?
2) Sample dataset: I’ll put together 10 tickets (sanitized) and send over by Monday 3/2.
3) PoC deployment model: We lean towards Private for PCI data, but if the hosted sandbox can guarantee no logs and dedicated tenancy for the PoC, we can consider it to move faster.

Wed 3/3 11:00 AM PT works for me — Rajiv, does that time work for you?

Best,
Jessie

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Jessie Carter <jessie.carter@finpay.com>, Rajiv Iyer <rajiv.iyer@finpay.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-02T09:18:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Discovery recap & PoC plan — FinPay integration (tech notes)

Hi all —

Quick technical notes to help your engineering team:

- SDKs: We have first-class SDKs for Python and TypeScript. Example quickstarts: Python (requests-style client + async streaming) and Node (streaming + function call support).
- Endpoints: chat (streaming & non-stream), embeddings, and completions. Function-calling returns structured JSON you can map to your workflows.
- Model recommendation: For the PoC, start with rw-inference/13B-quant (balanced latency/cost). If you need lower mem footprint, we can provide a 7B quant variant.
- Performance knobs: continuous batching, KV prefix caching, and token quantization — we’ll tune these after we see your real token distribution.
- Rate limits & quotas: For the PoC we’ll provision a dedicated sandbox quota to avoid throttling.
- Networking: Hosted sandbox requires outbound TLS (443) to api.redwood.ai. For Private we’ll coordinate VPC peering and IAM roles; typical setup takes 3–5 business days.

Attached is a short integration checklist (fields we’ll need from your team: API host allowlist IPs, sample payloads, and a sample ticket export).
[Attachment: integration-checklist.csv]

Happy to jump on a short technical sync on Wed 3/3 at 11:30 AM PT if 11:00 ends up being too early — otherwise I’ll join the 11:00 slot.

— Dev
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
dev_patel@redwood.ai
